ev.q: CDC analyzed data from a sample of 817 youths aged 12–17 years who responded to the web-based YouthStyles survey in 2020.
Multivariable logistic regressions were used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (aORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and p-values (α = 0.05).
Among the youths surveyed, 73.6% reported exposure to loud sound at school for >15 minutes a day
Exposed to loud sounds at school every day/two to four times/week versus never/every few months
nearly one half (46.5%) reported exposure every day or two to four times per week
Students in the South were more likely to be exposed to loud sounds at school
were more likely to report that they were provided with hearing protection devices (aOR = 5.4; 95% CI = 3.3–8.9)
The current study used data from Porter Novelli’s 2020 YouthStyles

methods_quotes.q: The resulting data were weighted to match March 2019 U.S. Census estimates.
Multivariable logistic regressions were used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (aORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and p-values (α = 0.05).
The PROC SURVEYFREQ procedure of SAS was used for descriptive analysis.
researchers dichotomized student answers into two categories for student exposure
